title: Request Lifecycle — Content Upload
purpose: Full POST /api/v1/content lifecycle from client through Vite proxy, Express server, middleware chain (CORS, JSON parser, auth, upload), controller, service, R2 storage, DB insert, and notification
description: Complete trace of a content upload request: Client sends POST /api/v1/content with Bearer token and multipart files. In development, Vite proxies to localhost:5000. Express Server applies CORS check and JSON body parser (1100mb limit). The protect middleware extracts Bearer token, calls supabase.auth.getUser for JWT validation, fetches full user profile via findUserById, applies reshapeUserForApp for camelCase conversion, and checks impersonation header. Upload middleware (Multer) processes multipart files with MIME type filter and 1GB size limit per file (max 10 files). Content Controller extracts body fields, applies requireContentOwnership guard, delegates to Content Service which generates UUID filenames, uploads to Cloudflare R2 via storage service (s3.putObject), creates thumbnail (sharp for images, ffmpeg for video), inserts content record via ContentModel, and fire-and-forgets subscriber notification.

validationRules.rule: Bearer token required in Authorization header
MIME type must be image/*, video/*, or allowed audio types
Title and visibility required for content creation

businessRules.rule: Scheduled content stays in draft until publishDate
Subscriber notification is fire-and-forget — failures silently caught

securityConsiderations: JWT stored in localStorage — XSS attack surface
1GB memory buffer — entire file loaded in RAM before upload (OOM risk for large files)
Private R2 bucket requires signed URLs for access
No content moderation during upload (NSFW, copyright) — reactive only via reporting
Impersonation via X-Impersonating-User-Id header — admin can create content as any user
Auth middleware calls Supabase Auth twice per request (getUser + findUserById)
performanceConsiderations: 1GB memory buffer for file upload — potential out-of-memory with concurrent large uploads
Synchronous thumbnail generation blocks request until complete
No CDN caching layer — all content served via per-request signed URLs
Subscriber notification iterates all active subscribers — could be slow for creators with many fans
R2 upload has 3 retries with exponential backoff — adds latency on network issues

annotations.text: 1GB memory buffer — entire file loaded in RAM before upload. Risk of OOM for concurrent large file uploads.
Synchronous thumbnail generation — blocks request until both upload and thumbnail complete
No CDN cache layer — signed URLs generated per-request, every page load triggers R2 API calls
Only workflow with retry logic: R2 upload uses 3 attempts with exponential backoff (500ms, 1000ms, 2000ms)
